note: Rebuilt from OSM with the corrected pipeline (defects 29-34). NOT a reviewed model: Step 3 was answered by auto_review.py assisted. Supersedes ../uruguay_solved/, which predates the satellite-cache, cross-border and line-length fixes; both are kept so the two can be compared.
assumptions: LOAD_MODEL_METHOD=legacy_ridge; COUNTRY_DEMAND_MW=1350, NATIONAL_EXPORT_MW=0, COUNTRY_CAPACITY_MW=0 (none needed). MIN_TRANSMISSION_VOLTAGE_V=115000, +/-60 deg branch angle limit, everything else pipeline default. The stale satellite cache was refused, so NTL/GHSL come from the declared NZ proxy rather than from another bus set's measurements.
result: 187 buses, 281 branches (26 transformers), 35 generators, ONE island. DC and AC feasible. AC power flow converges: Vmin 0.900, Vmax 1.079, every bus inside [0.9, 1.1], losses 60.4 MW (4.5 %) on 1350 MW. constrained_dispatch.py reports full_case_validated: true.
changes_from_uruguay_solved: Same topology (187/281/35), because none of the fixes touches Steps 1-3. 14 coastal substations that the old cross-border test struck off the domestic total now carry load. The satellite cache built for a 166-bus tessellation is no longer merged onto this 187-bus one. 111 of 255 lines had their length raised to the distance between the substations they join, adding 934 km and lifting the smallest reactance from 6.3e-5 to 1.41e-4 pu; losses rise from 3.7 % to 4.5 % because the conductors are no longer shorter than the ground they cover.
